title: Best Audiobook Narrators and Producers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an audiobook narrator or producer: what the package should include, platform requirements, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: An audiobook needs a narrator whose voice suits the book, and production that meets the technical requirements of audiobook platforms. Many narrators record and edit from home studios. Projects go wrong when the narrator is chosen without an audition, the files fail platform checks, or rights and payment terms are unclear. This guide helps you plan an audiobook from audition to upload.

faq.q: How do I choose a narrator?
faq.a: Ask for a short audition reading a page from your book. It shows how the narrator handles your style, characters and names. Listen to several before choosing.
Audiobook platforms have rules on file format, loudness, noise level and chapter files. Check your platform's current requirements and share them with the narrator.
Agree in writing. Many narrators work for a fee per finished hour; some work for a share of royalties. Make sure you have the rights to distribute the audiobook.

faq.q: Should I send a pronunciation list?
faq.a: Yes. Names, places and unusual words should be listed with pronunciations. It saves re-recording.
It depends on the book length and the narrator's schedule. Recording, editing and checking take several times the finished length.
